correctness.rationale: Exact first-order conditions give \(y^{k+1}=bz^{k+1}\) after each completed update. On this invariant manifold, \(\rho r=b\,\Delta z\) and \(|s|=\rho|\Delta z|\), so every nonstationary residual ratio is exactly \(b/\rho^2\). The induced three-branch penalty map is therefore exact. Crossing the deadband cannot overshoot it for every starting penalty exactly when \(\tau\le\mu\); if \(\tau>\mu\), every \(\rho\in(\sqrt{\mu b}/\tau,\sqrt{b/\mu})\) yields a literal two-cycle. The state contraction factor \(q=(\rho^2+ab)/((a+\rho)(b+\rho))\) lies strictly in \((0,1)\). A standalone exact-rational checker replays these identities and representative phase-boundary cases.

originality.rationale: The residual-balancing rule, its scaling sensitivity, and the fixed-penalty optimum are all treated as prior work. The accepted claim is the exact adaptive penalty map on the scalar quadratic source family, its sharp universal finite-stabilization threshold, its explicit period-two obstruction, and the exact relation of its deadband to the known fixed-penalty optimum. Targeted semantic searches returned no implication-equivalent finding. A highly relevant 2024 quadratic adaptive-penalty paper was identified but not inspected in full, which remains the principal residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of McCann--Wohlberg (2024) was not inspected; it could contain an equivalent scalar special-case calculation not visible in its abstract.
The adaptive-ADMM literature is large, and differently phrased analyses of residual-balancing cycles may exist outside the inspected sources.
The deadband comparison is coordinate-scale dependent; this is a feature of the standard residual heuristic, not a scale-invariant performance theorem.

value.rationale: The final penalty need not be merely an implementation detail: the canonical heuristic is widely used and variable-penalty convergence discussions often rely on eventual stabilization. The theorem gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient threshold for universal finite stabilization on a natural scalar strongly convex quadratic, identifies a concrete penalty two-cycle beyond it, and proves that stabilization can still leave an arbitrarily poor relative asymptotic rate versus the known fixed optimum. These are structural diagnostics rather than a routine recomputation of convergence.
